description:
List innovation flags, strongest relationship first.

    Use this when you want links between claims rather than the claims themselves.
    Every flag includes flag_type, cross_domain, and summary. summary says why the claims are linked.
    flag_type is lexical_association for shared terminology with no substantive relation, scientific_connection for a conceptual or methodological relationship, contradiction for a stored disagreement, or innovation when the claims state a mechanism that could transfer. lexical selects the same weak rows.
    cross_domain is true when the claims have different primary domains. It is not a flag_type and does not raise strength.
    Older rows may still use cross_domain or research_hypothesis.
    strength is computed for that pair. It is not claim evidence strength. A weak lexical link stays low and remains when min_strength is omitted or 0.
    Returns flag id, domain, summary, strength, flag_type, cross_domain, connected_domain, the claim ids on each path, and a claims array in that same order.
    Each claims item has claim_id, statement, and evidence strength. Full evidence stays on get_evidence.
    connected_domain is the primary domain of the claim that does not match the flag domain.
    It is null when the claims share a primary domain.
    Optional cross_domain_only, when true, returns only flags whose connected_domain is set.
    Optional flag_type keeps one label, for example lexical.
    Repeated claim paths return once, keeping the strongest flag for that pair.
    Example: get_innovation_flags(domain="ai-ml", min_strength=0.5, limit=10).
    Example: get_innovation_flags(domain="quantum", min_strength=0, flag_type="lexical", limit=5).
    Example: get_innovation_flags(domain="consciousness", cross_domain_only=True, limit=10).

cross_domain_only.description: When true, return only flags whose connected_domain is set. Default false.
cross_domain_only.title: Cross Domain Only

domain.description: Restrict flags to one domain. Example: ai-ml.
domain.title: Domain

flag_type.description: Keep one flag_type. lexical and lexical_association are the same weak class. Empty returns every type.
flag_type.title: Flag Type

min_strength.description: Drop flags below this strength, from 0 to 1. Example: 0.5.
min_strength.title: Min Strength

offset.description: Number of hits to skip. Example: 0.
offset.title: Offset

name: get_innovation_flags

claims.description: Claims on this path, in claim_path order. Each item has claim_id, statement, and evidence strength.
claims.title: Claims

connected_domain.description: Primary domain of the claim that does not match this flag's domain. Null when the claims share a primary domain.
connected_domain.title: Connected Domain

cross_domain.description: True when the claims have different primary domains. Independent of flag_type.
cross_domain.title: Cross Domain

flag_type.description: Kind of link. lexical and lexical_association are shared terminology with no substantive relation. scientific_connection is a conceptual or methodological relationship. innovation is a transfer whose mechanism is stated in the claims. contradiction is a stored disagreement. Older rows may still say cross_domain or research_hypothesis.

summary.description: Short reason this pair was flagged. Use it to follow the link or skip it.
summary.title: Summary

FlagPathClaim.description: One claim on a flag path. Evidence and contradictions stay on get_evidence.
FlagPathClaim.title: FlagPathClaim

FlagType.description:
How a flag should be read. A missing value loads as lexical_association.

lexical and lexical_association are shared terminology with no substantive
relation. New rows store lexical_association. scientific_connection is a
conceptual or methodological relationship. innovation is a transfer whose
object and mechanism are stated in the claims. contradiction is a stored
disagreement. cross_domain remains a valid older label. New rows store a
cross-domain link on cross_domain, not as the type.
FlagType.title: FlagType
